speeches.speaker: Jim Chalmers
speeches.brief: Moved the Regulatory Reform Omnibus Bill 2025, proposing 60 measures across 28 acts and 13 government agencies to reduce compliance costs, improve access to services, enable information sharing, modernise document requirements and increase regulatory efficiency and productivity. Debate was adjourned.

speeches.speaker: Susan Templeman
speeches.brief: Supported the Regulatory Reform Omnibus Bill 2025, which contains 60 measures amending 28 acts, repealing two acts and affecting 13 Commonwealth agencies. Reported that it would reduce duplication through a 'tell us once' approach, enable digital citizenship evidence, simplify information sharing across Services Australia programs and revise childcare subsidy language for children needing wellbeing support. Debate was interrupted.

speeches.speaker: Claire Clutterham
speeches.brief: Argued that the Regulatory Reform Omnibus Bill 2025 would improve government services, reduce regulatory burdens and increase productivity through information sharing, simpler healthcare access, streamlined administration, fuel-security measures and renewable-energy reforms; the debate was adjourned and ordered to resume later.

speeches.speaker: Ted O'Brien
speeches.brief: Supported practical housekeeping measures in the Regulatory Reform Omnibus Bill 2025 but argued that it was not substantive reform, and sought removal of the proposed Greenhouse and Energy Minimum Standards Act change while supporting a government amendment addressing fuel security limits.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Leigh
speeches.brief: Summed up debate on the Regulatory Reform Omnibus Bill 2025, thanking members for their engagement and support, and said the bill would reduce red tape through reforms affecting 28 acts and 13 Commonwealth government agencies, including changes to fuel stockholding, service delivery and identity verification.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Leigh
speeches.brief: Moved a government amendment limiting reductions to 6 months at a time, then argued that bureaucracy had wrongly prevented Major Caitlin Pedel from accessing paid parental leave and urged more ambitious regulatory reform. The minister said the government was exploring expanded access for overseas-posted ADF personnel and would consider the Administrative Review Tribunal's decision.

speeches.speaker: Tim Ayres
speeches.brief: Introduced the Regulatory Reform Omnibus Bill 2025 and moved its second reading, arguing that its 60 measures would cut red tape, amend 28 Acts, repeal two Acts and improve 13 government agencies, including through better information sharing and streamlined services; debate was adjourned.
